title: Wittich: fiducia as rest in God is of the essence — remitted-certainty may be lacking
source_text: XLVI. Sed hic observandum est fiduciam apud Doctores Reformatos pluribus modis sumi, adeoque plures eorum, qui hac in parte diverse loquuntur, idem reapse inter se sentire: alios vero qui videntur eodem modo loqui, revera tamen quoad sensum inter se discrepare. Et Christophorus Wittichius quidem jam saepe memoratus, qui fiduciam ponit inter actus fidei essentiales, per fiduciam illam intelligit acquiescentiam cordis in Deo, ut authore & fonte salutis. Quod ut clarius reddat, dicit distinguendos esse diversos fiduciae actus. Et quatenus, inquit, per fiduciam intelligitur acquiescentia in Christo & Deo, tanquam unico fonte & authore salutis, tanquam sufficienti servatore omnibus ad se confugientibus, dico omnino ad fidei essentiam pertinere. Sed si per fiduciam intelligatur persuasio de remissione peccatorum, sive in praeterito, sive in futuro, dico posse esse fidem quae ea destituatur; sed praeterea addo, istos fideles esse infirmos. Et subjungit se hanc distinctionem primum didicisse olim ex Reverendo Widmario, celeberrimi Maresii collega. In Theologia pacifica, cap. 11. num. 139.
pass_a_gloss: But here it is to be observed that trust is taken in several ways among the Reformed Doctors, and so many of them who speak diversely in this part in very deed feel the same among themselves: while others who seem to speak in the same way nevertheless in truth differ among themselves as to sense. And Christopher Wittich indeed, already often mentioned, who places trust among the essential acts of faith, understands by that trust the heart's resting in God as the author and fountain of salvation. Which that he may make clearer, he says diverse acts of trust are to be distinguished. And insofar as, he says, by trust is understood resting in Christ and God as the sole fountain and author of salvation, as a sufficient Savior for all who flee to Him, I say it altogether pertains to the essence of faith. But if by trust is understood persuasion concerning remission of sins, whether past or future, I say there can be faith which is destitute of it; but I add besides, that those faithful are weak. And he subjoins that he first learned this distinction formerly from the Reverend Widmar, colleague of the most celebrated Maresius. In Theologia Pacifica, chapter 11, number 139.
pass_b_english: ‘Fiducia’ is used in several senses — apparent verbal disputes often hide real agreement (or reverse).
Wittich’s essential fiducia = heart’s rest in God as salvation’s author.
Rest in Christ as sufficient Savior for those who flee = of faith’s essence.
Persuasion of remitted sins (past/future) can be lacking — such believers are weak.
